summary: Microsoft's MCP server that lets AI assistants control a web browser through Playwright, using page structure instead of screenshots.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Playwright MCP is a Model Context Protocol server that gives AI models browser automation through Playwright. It lets an LLM navigate and interact with web pages using structured accessibility snapshots rather than pixel-based input.
sixtySeconds.problem: AI assistants can't use websites on their own. Playwright MCP gives them fast, reliable browser control without needing vision models.
whoFor: QA engineers exploring automated testing with AI
Users of Claude, Cursor, VS Code and other MCP clients
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for an official, lightweight browser MCP server that works in most MCP clients. For coding agents, Microsoft suggests the Playwright CLI with skills, which uses fewer tokens.
requirements: An MCP client such as Claude Code, VS Code, Cursor or Amp

overview: Most clients use the standard config: an mcpServers entry named playwright that runs npx @playwright/mcp@latest. Claude Code users can add it with one command.
It uses Playwright's accessibility tree, so it is fast and deterministic and needs no vision model.

MCP suits agent loops that need persistent state and rich page introspection; for coding agents, the separate Playwright CLI plus skills can be more token-efficient. The project is Apache 2.0 licensed.
limitations: Coding agents may prefer the Playwright CLI
